mainTopic: Why a בריה and a חתיכה הראויה להתכבד are not cancelled out, and the debate between רבה בר בר חנה and רב over a forbidden piece that gives flavor to kosher pieces.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. The גיד הנשה is not cancelled out because it is a בריה, a distinct thing of its own. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's next case, a piece of נבלה mixed with kosher pieces, and asks why the kosher majority doesn't cancel it out. It answers that a piece of meat fit to serve to honored guests is too important to be cancelled. Next, the גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach both the גיד and the piece, since each has a reason the other lacks. A new discussion follows. רבה בר בר חנה rules that a forbidden piece forbids the pot only if its flavor reaches everything. רב is stricter: a kosher piece that absorbs the flavor becomes נבלה and forbids all the pieces of its kind. רב ספרא challenges רב, and אביי answers that the forbidden piece was removed early. רבא then begins a second answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The sciatic nerve is a distinct entity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the גיד הנשה is not cancelled out because it is a בריה, a complete entity of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an earlier question: why isn't the forbidden גיד הנשה cancelled out by the large amount of permitted meat? The answer is that a בריה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a small forbidden item mixed into a lot of permitted food can be cancelled out (ביטול). A בריה is a complete, distinct thing with its own identity, so it is too significant to be cancelled out. This explains the משנה's ruling about the גיד הנשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete, distinct entity or creature; too significant to be cancelled out in a mixture
Is different
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids us to eat

phrases.english: A distinct entity is different.
phrases.notes: He means the גיד הנשה from the earlier question. Since it's a whole thing in its own right, it doesn't get cancelled out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about why the גיד הנשה is not nullified.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing category: a בריה has special significance that blocks ביטול.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the גיד should be cancelled out by the majority of permitted meat like any other forbidden mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בריה is significant and is never cancelled out.

steps.title: Quoting the mishnah about a piece of carcass meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a piece of נבלה cooked together with kosher pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a piece of an animal carcass, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, a forbidden piece of נבלה mixed with kosher pieces. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that if the forbidden piece cannot be identified, all the pieces are forbidden. The גמרא quotes only the opening words, signaling that it is about to examine this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece (of meat or fish)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat
Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: And similarly, a piece of an animal carcass, etc.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets just means 'etc.': the גמרא quotes only the start of the משנה's line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גיד הנשה case to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forbidden piece of נבלה mixed with kosher pieces: if it can't be identified, all pieces are forbidden.

steps.title: Why not cancel it out by majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the forbidden piece should be cancelled out by the majority of kosher pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be nullified by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the forbidden piece isn't simply cancelled out, since most of the pieces are kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when one forbidden item is mixed with many similar permitted items, the rule of ביטול ברוב lets the majority win. So why does the משנה forbid everything?

keyTerms.meaning: Nullification by majority: a minority forbidden item is cancelled out by a permitted majority
And let it be nullified

phrases.english: But let it be nullified by the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that all pieces are forbidden when the נבלה piece is not identified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since most pieces are kosher, the general rule of ביטול ברוב should permit the mixture.

steps.title: The question only works by one view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its question: the משנה makes sense if anything 'usually counted' isn't cancelled out, but not if only things 'always counted' are protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who said we learned 'anything whose manner is to be counted.' But according to the one who said we learned 'that which is counted,' what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that its question is not a problem for everyone. It is a problem only according to one of two opinions about the rule of items that are counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that an item sold by count is too important to be cancelled out. One view says this applies to anything that is ever sold by count (כל שדרכו), which would include pieces of meat. The other view limits it to items always sold by count (את שדרכו); pieces of meat don't qualify, so the question remains.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (according to one view)
Anything whose way is to be counted, even only sometimes: the broad view
That which is counted, meaning always sold by count: the narrow view
What can be said? (signals the difficulty remains)

steps.confusionAlert: The difference is only one word, כל versus את, but it changes everything. כל means 'anything ever sold by count' (broad), while את means 'only what is always sold by count' (narrow).

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said
we learned: 'anything whose manner is to be counted,'
phrases.notes: This is the rule that things sold one by one are important enough not to be cancelled out. This view reads it broadly.

phrases.english: but according to the one who said
we learned: 'that which is counted,'
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כֹּל שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִימָּנוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge from step 3 to only one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling, according to the narrow view (את שדרכו לימנות).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pieces of meat are not always sold by count, so according to the narrow view they should be cancelled out by majority.

steps.title: A piece fit for guests is significant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a piece of meat is different because it is fit to be served to honor guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: A piece is different, since it is fit to give honor with it before guests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question even for the narrow view: a piece of meat has its own importance because you could serve it to guests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if meat is not 'always counted,' a piece that is nice enough to honor guests with is significant on its own. That importance stops it from being cancelled out by the majority. This idea is called חתיכה הראויה להתכבד.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece fit to be served in honor of guests; too important to be cancelled out
Since, because
Guests

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up חתיכה הראויה להתכבד as its own reason that something is not cancelled out, separate from the rule about things that are counted.

phrases.english: A piece is different,
since it is fit to give honor with it
before guests.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי חֲתִיכָה הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיָה לְהִתְכַּבֵּד בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New category of significance: fitness to honor guests.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the narrow view, pieces of meat should be cancelled out since they are not always counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: A piece fit for guests is significant on its own and is not cancelled out.

steps.title: Why the mishnah needed both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why the משנה taught both the גיד and the חתיכה: from the גיד alone, we wouldn't know about the piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary: if it had taught us only the nerve, that is because it is a distinct entity, but a piece, say not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to teach both cases. If we only knew about the גיד, we might think a mere piece of meat can be cancelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גיד is protected because it is a בריה, which is a strong reason. A חתיכה is not a בריה, so without the משנה we would think it is cancelled out. This step gives the first half of the צריכותא; the reverse direction follows.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was necessary (to teach both cases)
It taught us
I would say not

phrases.english: And it was necessary,
for if it had taught us only the nerve,
that would be because it is a distinct entity,
but a piece, I would say not.
phrases.notes: Meaning: we'd think a piece is not important enough and does get cancelled out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining both reasons (בריה and חתיכה הראויה להתכבד), the גמרא shows why each case needed its own mention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גיד case alone would not teach the חתיכה case, since a בריה has a stronger reason not to be cancelled out.

steps.title: The Piece Alone Would Not Teach Us the Nerve, So Both Are Needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. If the משנה had only taught the piece of meat, we might think the גיד is cancelled out, so both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only the piece of meat, we would say it is not cancelled because it is fit to serve to guests. But a גיד is not something you serve guests, so we might say it is cancelled. That is why both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its explanation of why the משנה listed both the גיד הנשה and the piece of meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the גיד alone would not teach us about the piece. Now the reverse: the piece is protected because it is fit to honor guests, and the גיד has no such importance. Each case teaches something the other could not, so the משנה needed both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Both statements are needed because neither could be learned from the other.
To honor guests with it. This is what makes the piece important enough not to be cancelled.
The sciatic nerve (גיד הנשה), which is forbidden to eat.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה needed both cases. The piece is protected because it can be served to guests, and the גיד needed its own mention because it lacks that importance.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the piece,
since it is fit to give honor with it
before the guests,
but a nerve, I would say no.
phrases.notes: He means we might have thought the nerve does get cancelled out in the mixture.

phrases.english: It is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation begun in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the גיד and the חתיכה must be taught, because each has a reason the other lacks.

steps.title: A Forbidden Piece Only Forbids If Its Flavor Reaches Everything
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה teaches that a piece of נבלה or non-kosher fish forbids the pot only if its flavor spreads into the gravy, the residue, and the pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה taught publicly: a piece of נבלה or of non-kosher fish does not make the pot forbidden unless it gives its flavor into the gravy, the leftover residue, and the other pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה בר בר חנה gives a rule about when a forbidden piece makes a cooked mixture forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His test is taste. If the forbidden flavor cannot be tasted in the food, the food stays permitted. The flavor has to reach every part of the pot, meaning the gravy, the residue, and the pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was not properly slaughtered. Its meat is forbidden.
A non-kosher fish.
Gives flavor. The test for whether a forbidden item spoils a mixture.
Gravy or broth.
The thick residue or sediment at the bottom of the pot.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana expounded publicly:

phrases.aramaic: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל נְבֵלָה וְשֶׁל דָּג טָמֵא
phrases.english: A piece of an unslaughtered carcass or of a non-kosher fish
does not make it forbidden,
unless it gives flavor into the gravy
and into the residue and into the pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about non-kosher pieces cooked with kosher food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forbidden piece forbids the pot only if its flavor reaches the gravy, residue, and pieces.

steps.title: רב: The Flavored Piece Becomes נבלה and Forbids Everything
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees. Once the forbidden flavor enters even one piece, that piece becomes נבלה itself and forbids all the pieces, because they are the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב had his announcer stand up and taught: once the forbidden piece gives flavor to another piece, that piece itself becomes נבלה. It then makes all the pieces forbidden, because they are its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב publicly teaches a stricter view than רבה בר בר חנה on the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה needed the flavor to reach everything. רב says it is enough for the flavor to reach one piece, which then counts as נבלה. That new 'נבלה' piece is the same kind as the other kosher pieces, and same-kind pieces do not cancel it out, so everything becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Here this means the announcer who repeated the teacher's words aloud to the crowd.
The piece itself becomes נבלה. The flavored kosher piece is treated like the forbidden meat.
Its own kind, meaning the same type of food.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pieces. The 'piece that becomes נבלה' is the kosher piece that absorbed flavor, not the original forbidden piece.

phrases.english: Rav set up an announcer about it, and expounded:
Once it has given flavor into a piece,
the piece itself becomes an unslaughtered carcass,
and it forbids all of the pieces
because they are its own kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter opposing view to רבה בר בר חנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A kosher piece that absorbs forbidden flavor becomes נבלה and forbids all same-kind pieces.

steps.title: Why Does רב Need the Flavor at All?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks אביי: רב follows רבי יהודה that a mixture of the same kind is never cancelled. So the forbidden piece should forbid everything even without giving flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to אביי: whose view is רב following? רבי יהודה's, who says a food mixed with its own kind is not cancelled. If so, why does it matter that the piece gave flavor? Even without flavor, everything should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges רב's ruling by pointing to the opinion רב must be relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason, 'because they are its own kind,' only works according to רבי יהודה, who holds that same-kind mixtures are never cancelled. But by that view, the forbidden meat piece is itself the same kind as the kosher pieces, so it should forbid them directly. The step of 'giving flavor to one piece first' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind mixed with its own kind is not cancelled. This is רבי יהודה's view.
Now, since... An opening that sets up a challenge.
Why specifically this? It asks why a detail was mentioned if it does not matter.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Abaye:
Now, like whom did Rav say his teaching?
Like Rabbi Yehuda,
who says a kind mixed with its own kind is not cancelled.
Why specifically when it gave flavor?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כִּי לֹא נָתַן טַעַם נָמֵי!
phrases.english: Even when it did not give flavor, too!
phrases.notes: The forbidden meat is already the same kind as the other pieces, so it should forbid them directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of רב's ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement that the forbidden piece first give flavor to another piece.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יהודה, same-kind mixtures are never cancelled, so the forbidden piece should forbid all the pieces even without giving flavor.

steps.title: The Forbidden Piece Was Removed Before the Others Were Added
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רב means a case where the forbidden piece was taken out before the other pieces came into the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: what case are we dealing with here? One where he first removed the forbidden piece.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב ספרא's question by explaining the exact case רב was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden piece was cooked with one kosher piece and removed before the rest were added. So it never mixed with the other pieces directly. The only way they become forbidden is through the kosher piece that absorbed its flavor and became נבלה, which is why the flavor matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a ruling to a specific situation.
He first removed it. The forbidden piece was taken out before the other pieces were added.

steps.whatToRemember: רב needs 'giving flavor' only because the forbidden piece was already removed. The kosher piece that absorbed its flavor becomes the forbidden piece that is never cancelled among its own kind.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, with what are we dealing?
Where he first removed it.
phrases.notes: The forbidden piece came out before the other pieces were added, so only the piece it flavored is left to forbid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's need for flavor seemed pointless, since the forbidden piece should forbid its own kind directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden piece was removed early, so only the flavored kosher piece, now נבלה, can forbid the others.

steps.title: רבא begins a different answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens his own answer to רב ספרא's question, as an alternative to אביי's answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: רבא is about to give a second answer to רב ספרא's question. His actual words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already answered the question by describing a specific case, where the forbidden piece was removed early. When the גמרא brings in a new speaker with 'רבא said', it signals that he will settle the same difficulty another way. So keep רב ספרא's question in mind: why does רב need flavor to spread if a mixture of the same kind is never cancelled?

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of the same kind, like forbidden meat with permitted meat. This is the topic of the question רבא is answering.
Is not cancelled. רבי יהודה holds that a same-kind mixture is never cancelled.
Gives flavor. The forbidden food passes its taste into the permitted food.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second answer to the challenge in step 10, as an alternative to אביי's answer in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer (its content follows in the next text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ספרא thought that since רב follows רבי יהודה, the forbidden piece should forbid everything even without spreading flavor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. רבא's resolution appears in the text that follows.
